prompt: imagemagick remap colormap precision bit depth limit
answer:
ImageMagick’s `-remap` has a colormap-size limit rather than a separate remap precision limit:

- For Q16 and higher builds, `MaxColormapSize` is **65,536 entries**.
- In practice, ImageMagick supports at most **65,535 unique colors**; exceeding that may cause the colormap to be reduced or an allocation error.
- A colormap requiring roughly 65,536 colors may also need about **157 MB** of memory.
- `-depth N` specifies bits per channel. When reducing depth, higher-order bits are normally discarded; `-dither FloydSteinberg -depth 8` can distribute the quantization error instead.
- `-depth` affects pixel precision when writing/reducing depth; it is not a way to bypass the `-remap` colormap-size limit.

Sources: [Discussion #7525](https://github.com/ImageMagick/ImageMagick/discussions/7525), [command-line options](https://imagemagick.org/command-line-options/), [Issue #7569](https://github.com/ImageMagick/ImageMagick/issues/7569).
